name: Bootstrapped / Founder Cashflow
description: Funding company growth exclusively from founder savings, early operating profits, and re-invested cashflow.
prerequisites: Fast time to initial cashflow (<30 days)
disadvantages: Growth rate capped by cash generation
Personal financial risk for founders
Slower hiring
bestFitWhen: High margin software/services with rapid customer payment cycles and minimal upfront capital.
avoidWhen: Capital-intensive hardware, clinical trials, or winner-take-all markets requiring rapid land-grab.

name: Customer Prepayment / Paid Pilots
description: Financing product build directly from customer pilot deposits, annual up-front subscriptions, or custom integration fees.
disadvantages: Risk of becoming a custom consulting shop
Delivery obligations before code is mature
bestFitWhen: B2B niche software or workflow tools solving immediate high-pain compliance or operational problems.
avoidWhen: Consumer mass-market products where individuals expect instant self-serve.

name: Government / Horizon Innovation Grants
description: Public research grants, innovation vouchers, and technology development awards from regional or EU programs.
prerequisites: High technical novelty or strategic sovereignty
advantages: Subsidizes deep R&D and specialized equipment
disadvantages: Significant application effort (50-200 hours)
Slow review cycles
Strict cost reporting and audit requirements
bestFitWhen: Deep tech, green transition, sovereign AI infrastructure, or medical diagnostics with long R&D horizons.
avoidWhen: Standard SaaS needing rapid marketing money or startups with <3 months of runway.

name: Top-Tier Startup Accelerator
description: Intensive 3-month cohort program providing seed capital, mentor network, customer introductions, and demo day exposure.
prerequisites: Early MVP or validated customer insight
disadvantages: Fixed dilution regardless of prior traction
Intense time commitment
Cohort peer pressure
bestFitWhen: First-time founders or teams targeting global VC rounds needing rapid network acceleration.
avoidWhen: Bootstrapped regional businesses or teams already with deep investor access.

name: Domain Angel Investors / Operators
description: High-net-worth operators, domain executives, and serial founders investing personal capital via SAFE or convertible note.
disadvantages: Small individual check sizes requiring multiple syndications
Variable investor engagement
bestFitWhen: Pre-seed phase where specialized industry credibility, customer intros, and fast bridge capital unlock the next milestone.
avoidWhen: Founders seeking large institutional lead commitments or passive checks without domain value.

name: Pre-Seed SAFE / Convertible Note
description: Simple Agreement for Future Equity (Post-Money SAFE or Convertible Note) deferring formal valuation until priced round.

repaymentProfile.repaymentMechanism: Equity conversion upon qualified priced round

advantages: Low legal cost (€1k-€3k vs €15k+ for priced round)
Rapid closing with rolling investor checks
disadvantages: Cap-table overhang if stacking multiple uncoordinated SAFEs with different caps
Uncertain dilution until conversion
bestFitWhen: Early stage rounds up to €1M to fund product validation before establishing formal corporate share classes.
avoidWhen: Later-stage rounds or in jurisdictions where tax laws penalize non-share equity instruments.

name: Institutional Seed / Series A VC
description: Institutional fund lead taking 15–25% equity in a priced equity financing round to accelerate rapid hypergrowth.
prerequisites: Proven PMF / strong early repeatable growth
advantages: Substantial growth capital to hire senior talent
disadvantages: Significant equity dilution
Loss of unilateral control (board & protective provisions)
Pressure for 10x-100x liquidity outcome
bestFitWhen: High-growth software or market network with proven unit economics ready to scale customer acquisition aggressively.
avoidWhen: Lifestyle businesses, niche consulting, or startups where founder priority is maintaining 100% control.

name: Revenue-Based Financing (RBF)
description: Upfront capital repaid via a fixed percentage of monthly gross revenue (e.g. 5-10%) until a capped multiple (1.3x-1.8x) is reached.

repaymentProfile.repaymentMechanism: Percentage of monthly revenue until return cap

advantages: Payments flex down during slow months
disadvantages: Direct drag on monthly operating cashflow
Requires existing proven recurring revenue
bestFitWhen: Profitable SaaS or eCommerce businesses with predictable customer acquisition economics needing growth capital.

name: Venture Debt & Growth Credit
description: Senior term loan paired with minimal equity warrants, typically provided to VC-backed startups to extend runway between rounds.
prerequisites: Corporate entity with enterprise asset base
advantages: Extends runway by 4-6 months with minimal dilution (<2%)
disadvantages: Debt service obligations regardless of performance
Negative covenants on cash reserves and IP liens
bestFitWhen: Post-Seed or Series A companies with proven runway looking to defer next equity raise to achieve higher valuation.
avoidWhen: Pre-revenue companies without strong VC sponsorship.
